findings.body:
Switch from `execFile` (argv array) to `exec` (shell) plus direct interpolation of the new `filter` parameter creates a command-injection surface.

```suggestion
    execFile("convert", [src, "-filter", filter, "-resize", `${w}x`, "/tmp/out.png"], (e) => e ? rej(e) : res("/tmp/out.png"));
```

The template literal passes caller-controlled `filter` unquoted into the shell. Any value containing `;`, `&&`, `$(`, or backticks will execute arbitrary commands.

```suggestion
    execFile("convert", [src, "-filter", filter, "-resize", `${w}x`, "/tmp/out.png"], (e) => e ? rej(e) : res("/tmp/out.png"));
```

summary: Critical command-injection vulnerability introduced by switching from `execFile` (argv) to `exec` (shell) while interpolating an untrusted `filter` parameter directly into the command string.

verification.reason: The patch replaces execFile (argv, no shell) with exec and interpolates the new unsanitized `filter` string into a shell command, which is a real command-injection regression at critical severity.

The change switched from safe execFile to exec and interpolates the caller-supplied filter unquoted into a shell command (`-filter ${filter}`), so metacharacters can run arbitrary commands. That is a genuine critical command-injection defect.
